metaData.originalTitle: VAPD AgentKit：可组合 Agent 前端通用库实践
metaData.title: VAPD AgentKit: A Composable Frontend General-Purpose Library for Agents
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the VAPD AgentKit, a composable Agent frontend general-purpose library developed by the vivo team, based on a unified message model, Runtime Adapter, and frontend orchestration, designed to provide a unified conversational AI capability foundation for businesses like notes, knowledge bases, and project management.
metaData.summary: This article focuses on the VAPD AgentKit developed by vivo's internet project team, aiming to solve the problem of redundant development of conversational AI capabilities across three major business scenarios: notes, knowledge bases, and project management. The core design principles are 'Message as Protocol, Runtime Pluggable, Frontend Orchestratable, and Progressive Enhancement.' Architecturally, it shields backend differences through a unified message model (covering message types such as User, Assistant, Thinking, ActionExecution, Result); achieves backend agnosticism through the Runtime Adapter interface (supporting any streaming protocol like SSE, GraphQL, WebSocket); and manages context, tool calls, and Agent turn loops through the frontend orchestration layer (AgentKit Provider, useAgentChat, useChat Hooks). The article elaborates on the conversion mechanism between event streams and message models, the implementation of Agent turn loops and tool calls (useAgentAction), the design of UI interactions and Suggestions, and provides a minimal getting-started example (3 steps to integrate Chat). Finally, the article looks forward to evolution directions towards knowledge base Q&A (RAG) and integrated workflow intelligence, and identifies the next steps needed to improve capabilities for history records, checkpoints, and Human-in-the-Loop.

mainPoints.point: VAPD AgentKit achieves composability and backend agnosticism for Agent frontend capabilities through a three-tier architecture of 'Unified Message Model + Runtime Adapter + Frontend Orchestration'.
mainPoints.explanation: This architecture unifies backend streaming events into a standard frontend message model, uses Adapters to shield protocol differences like SSE and WebSocket, and the frontend orchestration layer manages context, tool calls, and the Agent loop, allowing UI components to focus solely on message rendering without concerning themselves with the data source.

mainPoints.point: The Agent turn loop and tool calls are centrally handled on the frontend, enabling declarative registration and idempotent execution of tools on the frontend.
mainPoints.explanation: The useChat Hook serializes streaming events, captures tool call events to trigger frontend-registered handlers (via useAgentAction), and injects the result back as a ResultMessage, forming a complete round-trip for tool calls. Furthermore, a handler is triggered only once for the same execution ID, ensuring idempotency.

mainPoints.point: VAPD AgentKit emphasizes progressive enhancement. Phase one only implements the Chat mode, but by pre-embedding threadId/runId, it reserves extension points for advanced capabilities like history records, checkpoints, and replay.
mainPoints.explanation: The design follows the principle of 'implementing the Chat mode as a foundation first,' but the message model and runtime already include threadId (session) and runId (current loop) fields, laying the groundwork for future capabilities like session persistence, checkpoint rollback, and multi-turn evaluation.

keyQuotes: Decode events returned from the backend into a unified frontend message model; the UI only consumes messages without caring about the source details.

As long as the backend can output in a 'stream' form (SSE, GraphQL, WebSocket, Fetch ReadableStream, etc.), the Adapter will convert it into the same AgentStreamEvent, making the frontend logic completely protocol-agnostic.
Using the 'Message Model + Runtime Adapter + Frontend Orchestration' approach, we have turned the Chat mode into a foundational layer that can be 'composed'.

relatedArticles.title: A Possible Path for OpenClaw to Land in Real-World Production Applications
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the successful experience of Coding Agents, this article proposes that for business Agents (like OpenClaw) to land in production, the key is to reconstruct the open, decentralized, and hard-to-rollback business environment into a visualized, relatively closed, verifiable, and recoverable engineering operation space, and provides a specific path including visualization, closure, verification, and rollback layers.

relatedArticles.title: DeepSeek-V4 Preview: Ushering in the Era of Million-Token Context for Everyone
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: DeepSeek releases the V4 preview, offering Pro and Flash versions with million-token context as standard, achieving open-source leadership in Agent, reasoning, and knowledge capabilities, and open-sourcing the model simultaneously.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: In-Depth Analysis of vivo's Activity System Globalization Practices
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the complete technical practices and architectural evolution of vivo's activity system during globalization, from internationalization (multi-language, multi-timezone, multi-tenancy, data storage) to global co-line (unified architecture, unified domain name, handling external dependency differences).

relatedArticles.title: A Practical Guide to 'Progressive Spec' for AI Coding in 2026
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes a 'Progressive Spec' framework for AI coding environments, leveraging structured documentation to drive AI collaboration and balance development standards with execution efficiency.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: By evolving from Presto wide tables to Bitmap pre-computation and finally to a StarRocks storage-compute integrated architecture, the vivo marketing automation platform achieved a 10x improvement in query performance, a 93% reduction in resource costs, and ensured data security compliance.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth breakdown of the architectural design of mainstream Agents like OpenClaw and Claude Code, analyzing the pros and cons of key decisions across four dimensions: context management, tool loading, tool discovery, and main loop design.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the practical experience of the vivo community in introducing the AVIF image format through a CDN edge caching and server-side asynchronous transcoding solution, achieving an additional 20%+ reduction in image size compared to WebP, which had already been fully adopted.
